sections.h2: Where is Decatur, Alabama, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Decatur sits on Wheeler Lake, a stretch of the Tennessee River in north Alabama, and it is the largest city and the county seat of Morgan County. A small piece of the city crosses the river into Limestone County, between U.S. 31 and I-65.

The 2020 census counted 57,938 residents. The city covers about 61 square miles, roughly 54.6 of it land, and it lies about 25 miles southwest of Huntsville and 86 miles north of Birmingham, according to Wikipedia's Decatur entry.

Locals divide town into four quadrants. The CSX main line splits east from west, and Moulton Street splits north from south. That grid matters when you describe a house to a buyer, because street patterns, zoning and building styles differ from one side of the tracks to the other.

Two towns were glued together to make the Decatur of today. The original Decatur grew up around a ferry landing and the first railroad west of the Appalachians, and a second town, New Decatur, was founded in 1887 west of the tracks by newcomers from northern states.

New Decatur was renamed Albany in 1916, and the two cities merged in 1925 after a push to get a bridge across the Tennessee River in place of the ferry. Old Decatur and Albany still show up as neighborhood names on the northeast side.

The city also lays claim to the largest Victorian-era home district in Alabama. Union forces ordered nearly every building in town destroyed early in the Civil War, and only a few survived, including the Old State Bank and the Burleson-Hinds-McEntire House. Owners of century-old houses here often face roof, wiring, foundation and plumbing questions that scare off buyers who need a bank loan.

  • Older core: Old Decatur, Albany, Downtown and the riverfront Harborview area.
  • Southeast: Point Mallard Estates, Indian Hills, Burningtree Mountain, Cedar Lake and Hickory Hills.
  • Southwest: Westmeade, Austinville, Oak Lea, Moulton Heights and Autumn Ridge, among many subdivisions.

Decatur is an industrial river port, and its housing market follows plant hiring. The Port of Decatur handles barge traffic on the Tennessee River, and the employers listed for the city include General Electric, 3M, Wayne Farms, United Launch Alliance, Nucor, Bunge, Daikin, Hyosung, Ascend Performance Materials and the Tennessee Valley Authority.

United Launch Alliance builds rockets in Decatur and ships them by water to Cape Canaveral. Decatur General Hospital, a 273-bed hospital, is the third largest employer in Morgan County.

The city sits in the Huntsville-Decatur combined statistical area, a region known for engineers and aerospace work. A plant announcement or layoff can move a family quickly, which is why some owners need to sell on a short timeline.

sections.h2: What does Decatur's weather mean for a house?
sections.html:
Decatur has a humid subtropical climate, with about 53.4 inches of rain a year and 51 to 52 days at or above 90 degrees. Those numbers come from the climate normals summarized in the Wikipedia article.

Severe thunderstorms bring damaging wind, large hail and tornado risk, mostly in spring, with a second severe season that peaks in November. Remnants of Gulf hurricanes sometimes bring strong wind or heavy rain between July and October.

For a seller, that points to a short list of items buyers and inspectors check first:

  • Roof age and any hail or wind damage that was never repaired.
  • Gutters, grading and crawlspace moisture after a rainy December, the wettest month on average.
  • Water staining around chimneys, skylights and window frames.
  • Air conditioning age, since summers are hot and humid.

A house with an open insurance claim or deferred storm repairs can stall on an ordinary listing. A cash buyer prices those repairs in and skips the insurer's underwriting.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit affect where Decatur houses sell?
sections.html:
Most Decatur commutes run on U.S. 31 (6th Avenue), U.S. 72 Alternate (State Route 20), State Route 24 and State Route 67, which includes the Beltline Road that partly circles the city. I-65 passes east of town, and I-565 begins northeast of Decatur and connects to Huntsville.

The twin-span Steamboat Bill Memorial Bridge carries U.S. 31 and U.S. 72 Alternate across the Tennessee River. Two airports serve the area: Huntsville International and Pryor Field Regional.

Public transit is limited. NARCOG Transit runs demand-response service, and there is no fixed-route bus. Without fixed bus routes, a buyer without a car has few options, so a house's distance from the main roads is worth mentioning when you describe it.

sections.h2: What are the steps to sell a house in Decatur?
sections.html:
A Decatur sale closes when the deed is recorded with the probate judge, and Alabama requires the recordation tax to be paid before a deed is accepted. Under Alabama Code section 40-22-1, the tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, and the deed must come with a form attesting to the actual purchase price.

Morgan County's probate office handles most Decatur parcels, but the part of the city in Limestone County records there. Check which county holds your parcel before you sign anything.

The usual sequence looks like this:

  • Gather the deed, any mortgage payoff statement and a list of known repairs.
  • Confirm who must sign: every owner on the deed, and a personal representative if an owner has died.
  • Choose a closing agent, who runs the title search and prepares the closing statement.
  • Pay off liens and any unpaid property tax from proceeds.
  • Record the deed with the probate judge.

sections.h2: When are Decatur property taxes due?
sections.html:
Alabama property tax is due October 1 and becomes delinquent after December 31, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue. That rule applies to Decatur houses in either county.

If you sell in the fall or winter, ask your closing agent how the year's bill will be handled. A bill that is already due can be paid from your proceeds at closing, and an unpaid prior year can become a lien the buyer will want cleared.

sections.h2: What do Decatur sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
The most common problems are age, repairs and timing. Decatur has a long housing history, and owners of older houses often put off big jobs until it is time to move.

  • Inherited houses where the heirs live in other states and no one wants to manage repairs.
  • Rentals with worn-out units and tenants who are hard to move out.
  • Houses with storm damage, old roofs or deferred repairs.
  • Owners facing a job change tied to a plant or the Huntsville area.

A cash sale does not remove the title work, but it can remove showings, appraisal gaps and repair negotiations. If that fits your situation, the form on this page is the quickest way to start.

faqs.q: How many people live in Decatur, Alabama?
faqs.a: Decatur had 57,938 residents at the 2020 census. The city spans Morgan County and a small part of Limestone County.

faqs.q: Do I pay a tax to record my deed in Decatur?
faqs.a: Yes, Alabama charges a recordation tax of 50 cents per $500 of value on deeds, and it must be paid before the probate judge records the deed. Your closing agent usually collects it as part of the closing statement.

faqs.q: When is property tax due on a Decatur house?
faqs.a: The tax is due October 1 and is delinquent after December 31, per the Alabama Department of Revenue. Closing agents typically settle the current year between buyer and seller on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Which county records a Decatur deed?
faqs.a: Most of Decatur is in Morgan County, so most deeds go to that county's probate office. A small part north of the river is in Limestone County, so confirm where your parcel lies.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Decatur house with storm or roof damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Decatur has a spring and November severe weather season with hail and wind, and damaged houses sell regularly. Cash buyers evaluate the house as it stands, so you do not have to complete repairs first.
